citations.title: The Perceptron: A Probabilistic Model for Information Storage and Organization in the Brain
Gradient-Based Learning Applied to Document Recognition
Representation Learning: A Review and New Perspectives

claims.statement: Rosenblatt framed the perceptron as an adaptive probabilistic organization for recognition and generalization, a broader historical program than the later textbook shorthand of one linear classifier.
claims.scope: Rosenblatt's 1958 model, terminology, and stated research questions

claims.statement: Rumelhart, Hinton, and Williams showed how error derivatives could train multilayer connection weights so hidden units developed task-useful internal representations.
claims.scope: the differentiable networks and examples studied in the 1986 paper, without a solitary-invention claim

claims.statement: The 1998 document-recognition system demonstrated that local connectivity, shared weights, subsampling, and gradient learning can cooperate in an end-to-end task pipeline.
claims.scope: the architectures, datasets, and document-recognition tasks reported in the paper

claims.statement: Representation learning studies objectives and architectures that make useful factors easier for downstream tasks to use, but it supplies no task-independent definition of a universally good representation.
claims.scope: the methods and open questions surveyed by Bengio, Courville, and Vincent

claims.statement: Neural learning redistributes design among architecture, objective, data, optimization, and evaluation rather than eliminating design through automatic feature discovery.
claims.scope: a curriculum synthesis across the cited research programs

uncertainty: The history of reverse-mode differentiation and neural-network training has multiple lineages that a four-source packet cannot exhaust.
Later terminology such as deep learning and representation learning can make earlier authors appear to share a single modern program.
Internal units can support reliable predictions without admitting one stable semantic interpretation.
limitations: The packet omits recurrent networks, unsupervised pretraining, residual networks, normalization, modern optimizers, and much of neuroscience.
It does not derive backpropagation step by step or reproduce the cited experiments.
Historical influence, mathematical priority, biological plausibility, engineering utility, and present-day deployment safety are distinct claims.
